answer: I would like to talk about a friendship that has taught me a lot about the wider world. A person from a different culture whom I know well is a friend from university who grew up in Turkey. She came to our university in Bangladesh for a year as an exchange student, and we were in several of the same classes. Her home town is Izmir, on the Aegean coast, and she has shown me so many photos that I feel I almost know it. Getting to know her has been genuinely [[eye-opening]], because our backgrounds are quite different in some ways yet surprisingly similar in others. She has taught me a great deal about her country's food, festivals and customs, which I find fascinating. What I appreciate most is how her perspective has broadened my own; she often challenges assumptions I did not even realise I held. Our conversations are always [[enriching]], and we enjoy comparing how our two cultures approach things like family and hospitality. We even discovered that our families celebrate Eid in quite similar ways. As for how I feel about the friendship, I think friendships across cultures are especially valuable, because they quietly [[break down stereotypes]]. She is warm, curious and completely without prejudice, which makes her wonderful company, and we still video call every couple of months. Honestly, knowing her has made me more [[open-minded]], and it has confirmed my belief that people everywhere have far more in common than we tend to assume.

followUps.q: Would you like to visit her country?
followUps.answer: Very much. She has invited me to Istanbul and Izmir many times, and I would love to see the historic mosques and try the food she always talks about. Hopefully I can go within the next few years.

followUps.q: Is it easy to make friends with people from other cultures?
followUps.answer: It can take a little more effort at first, because of language and different customs. But once you get past that initial [[awkwardness]], I think those friendships are often especially close and rewarding.
